reason: I've had a dry cough for two weeks.
diagnosis: Likely ACE-inhibitor–induced dry cough from newly started ramipril, given the dry persistent cough beginning after ramipril initiation, absence of infectious or cardiopulmonary symptoms, and otherwise reassuring history.
keyPoints: Onset and timing relative to starting ramipril or other ACE inhibitor
Cough character: dry vs productive, blood, nocturnal pattern, triggers
Infectious and COVID symptoms/exposures: fever, sore throat, runny nose, sick contacts, travel
Red flags: dyspnea, wheeze, chest pain, hemoptysis, weight loss, night sweats
Smoking history and other lung risk factors, including COPD/asthma
Medication history and allergies, especially ACE inhibitors and recent new drugs
Alcohol use and general medical history
manner: slightly anxious, cooperative, gives brief answers
